subject: zoology
intro: Zoology is the science of animals — their origins, physiology, behaviour and conservation — and it leads to work studying wildlife, managing habitats and teaching the animal kingdom.

roles.title: Zoologists and Wildlife Biologists
roles.what: Study the origins, behaviour, diseases, genetics and life processes of animals and wildlife, collecting and analysing biological data to judge how present and potential uses of land and water habitats affect them.
roles.where: The phyla-by-phyla survey through the chordates builds the anatomical and taxonomic fluency fieldwork assumes, and the physiology unit's thermoregulation and osmoregulation underpin habitat assessment.

roles.title: Conservation Scientists
roles.what: Manage, improve and protect natural resources so they can be used without damaging the environment, conducting soil surveys, planning erosion control and advising land managers on sustainable practice.
roles.where: The behaviour, ecology and conservation unit — ethology, zoogeography, extinction and conservation — plus comparative physiology's adaptation topics supply the wildlife-management reasoning this work runs on.

roles.title: Biological Science Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach courses in the biological sciences, from introductory animal diversity to advanced ecology, often combining classroom teaching with research on the systems they cover.
roles.where: The course's arc — body plans, the protostome and deuterostome radiations, fishes through mammals — is the core content of university animal-biology teaching, already sequenced lecture by lecture.

roles.title: Biological Technicians
roles.what: Assist biological scientists by setting up instruments, monitoring experiments, collecting data and samples, and calculating and recording results — in wildlife work that means specimen handling, field data and lab analysis.
roles.where: Comparative anatomy and physiology give you the specimen literacy, and the ecology unit's data-driven treatment of populations and extinction risk matches the collecting-and-recording work of the role.
